attack.reasoning: The updates report widespread service disruption and a recurrence, but do not say whether hostile action contributed or rule it out. The available evidence is insufficient to classify this as an attack or not an attack.

findings.claim: The first incident was reported as affecting Actions, Git Operations, and Pull Requests; Webhooks and Issues were subsequently reported degraded as well.
The provider reported widespread impact across GitHub services from 15:06 to 15:16 UTC, and said systems were recovering.
Service-level degradation and recovery updates continued after the stated widespread-impact window; by 15:58 UTC the provider reported full recovery across all systems.
At 16:23 UTC the provider said the root cause had been identified and mitigations were being applied, but did not state the cause in that update.
A second widespread impact window, from 16:52 to 17:01 UTC, was described by the provider as a recurrence of the earlier incident; durable mitigation was in progress.
By 18:00 UTC the provider said mitigations had been applied and it did not anticipate another recurrence; the incident was resolved at 18:04 UTC.
The public updates establish that the provider identified a cause, but do not disclose enough technical detail to reconstruct it.
The recurrence indicates that the measures in place after the first incident were not yet a durable prevention; the provider itself said durable mitigation was in progress.

timeline.event: Beginning of the first widespread-impact window, as reported retrospectively by the provider.
The provider opened the first incident with reports of degraded availability for Actions, Git Operations, and Pull Requests.
End of the first widespread-impact window; the provider said systems were recovering.
The provider said degradation affecting Git Operations and Webhooks had been mitigated.
The provider reported full recovery across all systems while continuing to investigate the cause of the disruption.
The provider said the root cause had been identified and mitigations were being applied to prevent recurrence.
The first incident was marked resolved.
Beginning of the second widespread-impact window, later described as a recurrence of the earlier incident.
End of the second widespread-impact window; the provider said all systems had recovered.
The provider opened an investigation into new reports of degraded performance affecting Actions, Git Operations, Issues, and Pull Requests.
The provider said all systems had recovered, mitigations had been applied, and it did not anticipate another recurrence.
The second incident was marked resolved.

root_cause.claim: The specific technical root cause cannot be reconstructed from the available public updates. The provider said it had identified the cause, but did not name it in the evidence provided.

contributing_factors.claim: The first mitigation was not yet durable enough to prevent a recurrence; the provider reported the recurrence and said durable mitigation was in progress.

open_questions.question: What was the underlying technical cause the provider said it had identified?
open_questions.why_open: The updates say the cause was identified but do not describe it.

open_questions.question: What mechanism caused the disruption to affect multiple GitHub services?
open_questions.why_open: The updates list affected services and impact windows but do not explain their dependency or failure mechanism.

open_questions.question: Why did the disruption recur after the first incident was marked resolved and mitigations were being applied?
open_questions.why_open: The provider calls the second incident a recurrence and says durable mitigation was in progress, but does not explain why the initial measures did not prevent it.

open_questions.question: Did deliberate hostile action contribute to either impact window?
open_questions.why_open: The updates do not state whether an attack occurred or rule one out.

tool_calls.name: search_library
tool_calls.query: Prior outage postmortems involving widespread degradation across many GitHub services, short periods of broad impact with recovery and recurrence, where updates initially say root cause under investigation; identify reported underlying causes and signals to look for.
